descriptors.definition: Winding up encompasses both formal winding up under the Companies Act, 2013 and liquidation under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. Provisions allowing applications based on inability to pay debts have been omitted from the Companies Act, 2013 framework.
inclusion: Winding up procedures governed by the Companies Act, 2013
Liquidation procedures under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
exclusion: Applications for winding up strictly on grounds of inability to pay debts under the 2013 Act
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes traditional company law winding up from modern insolvency liquidation mechanisms.

descriptors.definition: Part I of Chapter XX of the Companies Act, 2013 governs the winding up of a company specifically by the Tribunal. This statutory mode establishes the core procedural rules for tribunal-led corporate dissolution.
inclusion: Winding up administered directly by the Tribunal
exclusion: Voluntary winding up modes outside tribunal oversight
nearby_distinctions: Focuses exclusively on tribunal-administered winding up rather than alternative liquidation pathways.

descriptors.concept_name: Circumstances In Which Company May Be Wound Up By Tribunal [Section 271]
descriptors.definition: A company may face tribunal-ordered winding up under specific statutory grounds including special resolutions, actions against state integrity, fraudulent affairs, default in filing financial statements for five consecutive years, or when deemed just and equitable. These diverse statutory triggers ensure judicial intervention for severe corporate malfeasance or deadlock.
inclusion: Winding up via special resolution
Actions harming state security or public order
Fraudulent formation or management
Consecutive five-year financial statement filing defaults
Just and equitable grounds
exclusion: Petitions based solely on commercial debt defaults omitted under current framework provisions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes objective statutory defaults like non-filing from subjective judicial assessments like the just and equitable standard.

descriptors.definition: Authorized stakeholders including the company, contributories meeting holding duration criteria, the Registrar, or Central/State Governments may formally present a winding up petition to the Tribunal. Registrars require central government sanction after offering the company a representation opportunity.
inclusion: Petitions by the company accompanied by a statement of affairs
Contributory petitions meeting six-month holding thresholds
Registrar petitions with prior government sanction
exclusion: Registrar petitions grounded in special resolution winding up
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates standing requirements across stakeholders, imposing strict holding duration rules for contributories and sanction rules for the Registrar.

descriptors.definition: Upon receiving a winding up petition, the Tribunal possesses discretionary powers to dismiss it, issue interim orders, appoint a provisional liquidator, or order definitive winding up within ninety days. The Tribunal cannot refuse a winding up order solely because company assets are mortgaged or entirely absent.
inclusion: Dismissal of petition with or without costs
Appointment of provisional liquidator after notice
Issuance of winding up orders regardless of asset encumbrance
exclusion: Refusal of winding up orders based exclusively on asset deficiency or heavy mortgage
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts interim relief and provisional measures with final winding up orders and alternative remedies.

descriptors.concept_name: Directions For Filing Statement Of Affairs [Section 274]
descriptors.definition: When a third-party petition establishes a prima facie winding up case, the Tribunal directs the company to submit its objections and statement of affairs within thirty days, extendable by another thirty days. Non-compliance results in the forfeiture of the right to oppose the petition alongside penal consequences for responsible officers.
inclusion: Mandatory filing of objections and statement of affairs by the company
Submission of completed and audited books of account to the liquidator within thirty days of winding up orders
exclusion: Petitions initiated directly by the company itself under section 272
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates obligations triggered by external petitioner filings from voluntary company-initiated applications.

descriptors.definition: The Tribunal appoints an Official Liquidator or an insolvency professional from a maintained panel as the Company Liquidator during a winding up order. Appointed liquidators must file a conflict of interest declaration within seven days and operate under terms specified by the Tribunal.
inclusion: Appointment of panel insolvency professionals as company liquidators
Filing of mandatory independence declarations within seven days
exclusion: Appointment of liquidators outside recognized statutory panels or without tribunal specification
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes provisional liquidator appointments made prior to final orders from permanent company liquidator appointments.

descriptors.definition: The Tribunal may remove a provisional or company liquidator for recorded causes such as misconduct, fraud, professional incompetence, or persistent conflicts of interest after providing a reasonable hearing. Tribunals can also recover loss or damage caused to the company directly from responsible liquidators.
inclusion: Removal based on lack of independence or diligence
Financial recovery of loss or damage from culpable liquidators
exclusion: Removal without recording written causes or denying a reasonable hearing opportunity
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts routine vacancy transfers due to death or resignation with punitive removals driven by professional default or misconduct.

descriptors.concept_name: Intimation To Company Liquidator, Provisional Liquidator And Registrar [Section 277]
descriptors.definition: The Tribunal must intimate winding up or provisional liquidator appointment orders to the liquidator and Registrar within seven days. The Registrar updates records, notifies the Official Gazette, and informs relevant stock exchanges for listed entities, while the winding up order operates as a discharge notice for employees.
inclusion: Gazette notification and stock exchange intimations by the Registrar
Constitution of a winding up committee within three weeks of the winding up order
exclusion: Discharge of employees when corporate business operations are expressly continued
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates general record updates from specialized stock exchange disclosures required exclusively for listed corporate entities.

descriptors.definition: A winding up order operates collectively in favour of all creditors and contributories as though issued on a joint petition filed by them. This ensures equitable distribution and unified representation of stakeholder interests.
inclusion: Collective legal operation benefiting all company creditors and contributories equally
exclusion: Exclusive individual legal enforcement benefits favoring isolated creditors post-order
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts individual creditor enforcement actions with unified statutory benefits operating on behalf of the entire creditor and contributory body.

descriptors.concept_name: Stay Of Suits, Etc. On Winding Up Order [Section 279]
descriptors.definition: Following a winding up order or provisional liquidator appointment, no new suits or legal proceedings may be commenced against the company without tribunal leave, and pending proceedings require tribunal permission to proceed. However, this restriction explicitly excludes any proceedings pending in appeal before the Supreme Court or a High Court.
terminology: appeal before Supreme Court or High Court
inclusion: Mandatory tribunal leave for commencing new suits or continuing pending primary court proceedings
Unrestricted continuation of appeals pending before High Courts or the Supreme Court
exclusion: Initiation of original legal actions without prior tribunal permission
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes ordinary pending trial suits requiring tribunal leave from appellate proceedings before higher constitutional courts requiring no such leave.

descriptors.definition: The Tribunal holds comprehensive jurisdiction to entertain and dispose of all suits, claims, fast-track merger applications, and questions of law or fact relating to company assets and winding up matters. This jurisdiction applies regardless of whether the underlying proceedings or claims arose before or after the winding up order.
inclusion: Suits, claims, and branch-level claims by or against the company
Adjudication of priority questions and asset obligations related to winding up
exclusion: Matters completely unrelated to corporate winding up obligations or statutory exceptions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes exclusive tribunal oversight over winding up disputes from normal civil court jurisdictions.
